recommendations.text: Keep the 80% hourly rise cap for PAPER. It is not a proven optimum. A 20% relative relaxation would be 96%, which allows a more extended chase. Round-trip fees on the $47.50 ticket are about $1.71 (about 3.6%) and slippage is not modeled, so a name that has already risen most of that hour still needs more than the fee drag in further upside before fee-adjusted P&L is positive. That figure is not profit. Analyst chase already rejects roughly above 24% hourly (max_chase 0.30 times chase_h1_pct 80) without moving the 80% scanner cap.

Do not lower the $20k liquidity floor. On the 23:47 Stockholm board, every in-cap name was missing liquidity or under $20k, and those under the floor also failed buy-pressure or were not steadily rising. A blind 20% cut to $16k would not have produced an early-momentum qualifier on that board.

Keep top 10 at 35, including the auditor. Concentration rejects are unsafe, not a scanner knob to loosen. Scanner equality now uses the auditor's existing boundary (35 rejects) so the number itself is unchanged.

Keep alive_volume_h1 25000, organic_buys_h1 150, and min_score 70. The archived funnel did not attribute analyst failures to one of these, so a 20% cut would be blind. Rising names get flush=0, and the four published minimums then score about 51, under 70. That interaction is visible in the score; it was not changed.

Proposed strategy-only exit: arm a trail after +8% gross with a 4% giveback from the peak, plus a two-print momentum deterioration exit. Stop and liquidity-pull stay. Default off so exit risk is unchanged until you approve it. Existing trail remains +20% / 12%.
